boundary.writeGate: configure() raises _StagingOwnershipUnproven before the first credential write when the descriptor-to-entry binding cannot be established.
boundary.publicationGate: The trusted-parent precondition is re-verified, the ownership evidence is re-derived, the pre-rename binding is re-checked, and the pinned directory is required to hold exactly the entries this run acquired, each still resolving to the identity it was acquired under AND to the SHA-256 of the bytes this run wrote into it. A name this run acquired that has disappeared is reported as a loss of its own, apart from an injected or replaced entry. A directory that cannot be enumerated is refused rather than published on the strength of its inode alone. That evidence is re-derived once more AFTER the rename, because the rename is a later step: a mismatch there raises _PublishedEntryNotOwned as detection after the fact, with this run's own files removed and a foreign entry preserved for manual cleanup.
boundary.rollback: Exact-owned: only acquired file identities are unlinked, and the directory is rmdir'd only while the cleanup name still resolves to the proven inode. The check and the rmdir are separate steps; what was removed is re-enumerated from the parent afterwards and reported as _CleanupTargetMismatch.
boundary.unauthenticatedWindow: The create-to-open window is not authenticated by pathname; the trusted parent (0700, current-user-owned, no additional ACL) is the precondition that excludes other principals. A same-account actor racing that window is not detected, and the README now says so.
boundary.wasPreviousState: staging_ownership_proven was hardcoded False and gated only rollback rmdir; credential writes and publication were not gated on ownership.
acknowledgedNotClosedWindows: create-to-open: not authenticated by pathname; not detected; both branches pinned by fixtures.

last re-derivation to renameatx_np: an entry changed or injected there is refused only after the rename published it (detection after the fact), with manual cleanup guidance and no automatic removal of the foreign entry.

rollback stat-to-rmdir: a same-account actor parking an empty directory under this run's unpredictable staging name makes this run remove that empty directory and leave its own behind. Darwin keeps an open descriptor's st_nlink at 2 after rmdir, so this is detectable after the fact by re-enumerating the parent, never preventable, and unconfirmed when the parent cannot be listed.
